comparison_policy: Never pool raw scores across benchmarks with different task sets, models, harnesses, judges, metrics or execution environments.
Store the observation date, model/harness context, task denominator, uncertainty interval and live-versus-historical page state for every result.
Treat browser-tool benchmarks as tool-operation evidence, not frontend code-generation evidence.
Reproduce native task splits and scorers before making superiority claims; preserve failed, blocked and unparseable runs in denominators.

comparators.name: Vision2Web
comparators.scope: Visual website development across static responsive pages, interactive multi-page frontends and full-stack applications; GUI workflow verification plus VLM visual judging.

observations.display: No results yet for this season

limitations: The 82.3 row is a historical snapshot, not a verified current-season leader.
Visual and functional level components are not directly comparable to SFEB's internal scorecard.
Official evaluation uses its own task set, submission format and current-season VLM/GUI judge.

comparators.name: Design2Code
comparators.scope: Screenshot-conditioned frontend reconstruction of real-world webpages, with automatic rendering metrics and human evaluation.

observations.metrics: automatic rendering metrics validated with human evaluation

limitations: Primarily measures screenshot-to-code visual reconstruction, not the complete functional, security, causal repair or maintenance loop.
Fixture and asset reuse requires a separate license and provenance review.

comparators.name: WebdriverIO Browser Agent Benchmark
comparators.scope: Browser-tool comparison: same model, harness and prompt while swapping browser tools; live website tasks judged by WebJudge.

observations.model_context: page lists two model contexts; the indexed aggregate row is not a model-independent result

limitations: The benchmark page's indexed October data shows published rows, while a direct page render on 2026-11-22 displayed an empty run-log state; retain this as an October historical snapshot, not a live leaderboard claim.
The 62% row aggregates 165 task observations; it must not be described as a clean 62/100 single-run result.
The benchmark reports roughly ±10 percentage-point intervals for 100 tasks and warns that overlapping intervals are not reliable rankings.
Live sites, bot blocks and CAPTCHAs reduce repeatability; WebJudge disagrees with human reviewers on about one run in seven.
This measures browser-tool effectiveness, not generated frontend quality.

comparators.name: SWE-Bench Pro task-quality audit
comparators.scope: Meta-evaluation of benchmark task validity: strictness, underspecification, test coverage and prompt correctness.
limitations: This is a task-quality audit, not an agent performance leaderboard.
The reported problem fraction applies to the audited SWE-Bench Pro public split, not to SFEB or Vision2Web.

comparators.name: Arena Code Arena — WebDev / Frontend
comparators.scope: Live pairwise human-preference arena for frontend web-app generation; anonymous model outputs are compared and users vote for the response they prefer.
limitations: This is a human pairwise-preference rating, not a deterministic task-success rate or independent functional oracle.
Vote count is not the number of unique independent benchmark tasks; prompts, users and comparisons are drawn from Arena traffic.
Model configuration, reasoning budget and harness labels are part of the submission identity; do not attribute the score to the base model alone.
Cost frontier values exist only for submissions with cost data; 49 listed models were not plotted due to insufficient cost data.
Do not compare Elo/rating values directly with Vision2Web scores, SFEB task rates or browser-agent success percentages.

comparators.name: Arena Code Arena — Image-to-WebDev
comparators.scope: Human pairwise-preference arena for generating working web experiences from visual references.
limitations: Human preference evaluates impressions of paired generated experiences, not requirement completeness or security invariants.
Ratings are specific to this Arena prompt distribution and model configuration; they are not comparable to the frontend WebDev or Vision2Web numeric scales.
Cost values are reported only for the displayed Pareto frontier submissions.

comparators.name: Arena Code Arena — Fullstack
comparators.scope: Human pairwise-preference arena for end-to-end web applications with backend/database/authentication/integration/deployment capabilities.
limitations: Human pairwise preference is not a production-readiness, reliability, security or test-coverage guarantee.
No task-count denominator is exposed on the cited leaderboard page; vote count must not be treated as unique task count.
Model scores are not directly comparable with frontend WebDev or Vision2Web.

comparators.name: Interaction-as-a-Judge
comparators.scope: Research method using computer-use agents to evaluate generated applications through interactions, alongside human preference and correctness labels.

observations.status: unresolved; paper and released-card counts are different snapshots/definitions and must not be conflated

limitations: The paper's 6,858 preference pairs and 222 correctness applications differ from the released dataset cards' 6,390 pairs and 189 app versions; the difference is unresolved and counts must be reported separately.
Reported gains are on the paper's specific data, models, judge configurations and protocols; they are not general frontend accuracy rates or SFEB results.
Human preference prediction and requirement correctness are distinct target variables.
Computer-use judges can miss states, be manipulated by page content or misinterpret task intent; deterministic and human-calibrated checks remain necessary.
The preference dataset card lists CC-BY-4.0 for user prompts but model outputs remain under provider terms; review component assets/privacy before reuse.

comparators.name: Arena Code Arena — HTML
comparators.scope: Human pairwise-preference board for HTML-oriented web-development submissions.
limitations: This is a human preference rating, not deterministic requirement completion.
Model configuration and Arena prompt distribution are part of the submission.
The HTML board is distinct from general WebDev/Frontend and React boards; do not pool ratings or votes.

comparators.name: Arena Code Arena — React
comparators.scope: Human pairwise-preference board for React-specific web-app development submissions.
limitations: This is a human preference rating, not deterministic requirement completion.
React-specific ratings do not represent Leptos capability; use as an ecosystem comparator, not a Rust framework benchmark.
Do not pool React and general WebDev ratings.

comparators.name: Arena Code Arena — WebDev overall
comparators.scope: Live pairwise human-preference arena for generated web applications; broader WebDev aggregate, distinct from frontend/HTML/React/Fullstack sub-boards.
limitations: Human preference rating, not deterministic task-success or requirement-correctness evidence.
The overall board and frontend/HTML/React/Fullstack sub-boards are separately calibrated; do not blend their ratings.
Vote count is not a count of unique benchmark tasks.
Model, configuration and reasoning budget are part of submission identity.
